candidates.admission_decision: Retain as an uncounted public candidate. Keep these three related items in one exposure family. Official split is unassigned.
closest_canonical: qcb-core-la-101 proves one particular inverse split sends a known signed pair to its norm and zero; qcb-core-sp-001 derives its sign convention. These give a local orbit, but neither recovers an unknown edge from probability reports.

qcb-core-sp-005 sums sibling squared norms across a prescribed marginal; qcb-core-la-104 grades unchanged outside rows, elimination and persistence in a prescribed sweep window. Here the cut index is an unknown to be inferred from before-and-after data.

qcb-core-la-016 distinguishes operator signs at equal probabilities; qcb-core-la-015 measures operator distance for known angles. qcb-core-la-215 prices the zero-pair branch of an angle routine. These supply sign and zero-case neighbors only.
candidates.closest_workbook: A1 proves normalization of a signed table. A4 and B3 bound differences of known rotations or optimize precision. B2 exposes a relative branch phase. None identifies an unknown adjacent pair from populations or tests whether any one gate fits.
candidates.assessment_overlap: V2 normalized_branch_born_aggregation shares summation of populations; coherent_control_global_relative_phase separates probabilities from coherent signs. V3 promise_register_protocols and sparse-v1 banded_sparse_address_semantics address register controls and addresses. Course v1–v5 marginal-norm-pythagorean and matrix-constructions-givens-determinant, plus the public pilot k-ry-half-angle-convention, cover the local algebra. The assessed inverse identification uses a family of ordered cuts.

neighbors.shared_subproof: Both aggregate information on blocks of coordinates.
neighbors.proof_difference: T3 projects amplitudes onto uniform leaf vectors and optimizes fidelity through signed means. This item compares measured sums of squares across path cuts and diagnoses the edge that could change them.

neighbors.shared_subproof: Both ask which hidden operations are compatible with supplied probabilities.
neighbors.proof_difference: W1 solves columnwise coefficient inequalities for a fixed permutation route and a scale. Here a circle of real amplitudes and fixed outside coordinates decide reachability by one gate.

neighbors.shared_subproof: A real half-angle rotation changes basis probabilities while retaining signs at amplitude level.
neighbors.proof_difference: B1n specifies the two gates and classifies entanglement and Bell-ray angles. Here the angle and edge are unknown, and the data concern two probability distributions on a path.

neighbors.shared_subproof: Both ask what measured populations can identify.
neighbors.proof_difference: B2n reconstructs density-matrix coherence from equatorial two-qubit settings. Here the inference is which adjacent edge reconciles populations; there is no unknown complex density-matrix entry.

candidates.shared_subproof: The selected pair moves on a circle through its signed input. Its squared radius is fixed. Unchanged coordinates and the same local circle law support both necessity of the observed cut pattern and sufficiency for either input sign.
candidates.decisive_difference: Identify all adjacent edges compatible with two population profiles using their cumulative sums, including observations which distinguish an edge and those which cannot distinguish any location.
candidates.full_credit_work: Derive the prefix test in both directions for every possible input sign, identify all compatible edge locations in the equal-profile and unequal-profile cases, handle a zero pair, and diagnose two exact datasets.

candidates.admission_decision: Retain as an uncounted public candidate. Keep these three related items in one exposure family. Official split is unassigned.
closest_canonical: qcb-core-la-101, qcb-core-la-103 and qcb-core-la-104 supply pair annihilation, reversed inverse lists and a bottom-up sweep. The graded LA104 outside-row and zero-persistence fragments, and LA103 inverse order, are reusable pieces of the upper bound. None lower-bounds every alternative circuit.

qcb-core-la-102 and qcb-core-la-106 use determinants for a square-matrix decomposition; qcb-core-la-105 pins a nonnegative isolated orthonormal pivot. Preparing one specified signed vector leaves the other columns free and makes a source-only sign change a separate boundary.

qcb-core-la-119 counts the full fixed selected-RY/Gray producer, including the full triangular list; qcb-core-la-203 charges the specified stored sweep, and qcb-core-la-215 charges the input-dependent angle routine. This item minimizes abstract two-level gate occurrences over all circuits.
qcb-core-sp-001 realizes signed pairs, and qcb-core-la-016 observes half-angle sign reversal. Neither depends on the locations of the initial site and target support.
candidates.closest_workbook: B1 propagates clean-column identities to a complete chronological run; A4 supplies the rotation convention and exact operator distance. B3 optimizes precision cost for a fixed list of gates. This item optimizes the list itself with free exact angles and a single prescribed column.
candidates.assessment_overlap: The public pilot r-decomposeSO-count-identity counts the fixed full-matrix sweep, and neg-givens-count-needs-SO-not-O distinguishes determinant signs. Course v1–v5 matrix-constructions-givens-determinant and the local pilot row-determinant slice use the same matrices. V2 coherent_control_global_relative_phase and normalized_branch_born_aggregation share sign and mass considerations. Neither those public clusters nor V3 promise_register_protocols or sparse-v1 banded_sparse_address_semantics supplies a sharp gate minimum for this single-vector path model.

neighbors.shared_subproof: A witness at a fixed coordinate can impose a lower bound on every competing construction; a matching construction proves optimality.
neighbors.proof_difference: W2 uses column absolute sums against caps in a weighted-permutation decomposition. This item counts individual path cuts through which target mass must travel and matches the bound by local rotations.

neighbors.shared_subproof: Both work with signed unit-vector coordinates indexed in order.
neighbors.proof_difference: T1 bounds differences of samples using a polynomial derivative and grid spacing. This item accepts arbitrary signed coordinates and asks how many exact gates are needed to create them.

neighbors.shared_subproof: Both specify an exact input and distinguish signed amplitudes from their probabilities.
neighbors.proof_difference: B1n classifies a fixed two-qubit gate sequence as the angle varies. The path problem varies the entire sequence and proves a universal lower bound from every required cut.

neighbors.shared_subproof: Both prove tightness by constructing a legal realization.
neighbors.proof_difference: The Bell item realizes a range of fidelities under given measurement constraints. This item realizes one specified vector using a minimum number of edges.

candidates.shared_subproof: A rotation moves mass only between its endpoints and its inverse restores any signed pair. The first fact yields one lower bound at each necessary cut. Local signed compression and reversal provide the construction independently.
candidates.decisive_difference: Find the exact minimum number of adjacent coordinate rotations taking a chosen basis vector to a specified signed vector, prove a lower bound against every circuit, and identify optimal source positions. G1s observes an unknown single gate; this item designs a shortest sequence.
candidates.full_credit_work: Identify all separating cuts forced by the target, show they impose additive gate lower bounds, construct a signed preparation on the intervening path including zero target entries, settle both source-only signs and the one-site obstruction, and optimize source placement on multisite supports.

candidates.proposed_use: Public study and proposed training, pending maintainer reconciliation of exposure and official split.
candidates.admission_decision: Retain as an uncounted public candidate. Keep these three related items in one exposure family. Official split is unassigned.
closest_canonical: qcb-core-la-213 bounds supplied primitive-wire scheduling depth by gate count. It neither synthesizes disjoint coordinate-pair layers nor optimizes over schedules. qcb-core-la-119 counts an unoptimized Gray compiler for a full matrix.

qcb-core-la-101, qcb-core-la-103, qcb-core-la-104 and qcb-core-sp-001 provide signed two-site compression, an inverse, zeroing for a fixed path window and a sign branch. They justify individual synthesis steps after scheduling; they do not compute an optimal reached subtree.

qcb-core-sp-005 supplies additivity of pair mass. The reserved qcb-core-plan-211 concerns splitting a sparse matrix support into matchings by edge coloring. Child-to-time matching here maximizes retained target mass subject to when each subtree can start.
candidates.closest_workbook: A3 uses clean-subspace projection and a normalized output, G2 bounds mass and target error for a fixed sequence of approximate isometries, and B3 optimizes precision for a fixed gate list. None characterizes which coordinate subspaces exact matching layers on a rooted tree can reach.
candidates.assessment_overlap: V2 normalized_branch_born_aggregation shares squared masses; internal_bond_phase_interference and the v1–v5 course marginal-norm-pythagorean cover coherent sums and pair mass respectively. The public pilot qs-resource-depth-parallel-vs-serial distinguishes serial and parallel resource arithmetic, while qs-prepare-ry-cx-counts counts a specific loader. V3 promise_register_protocols and sparse-v1 banded_sparse_address_semantics use different primitives. Here simultaneous operations are disjoint basis-level two-site rotations and the question optimizes over every legal schedule.

neighbors.shared_subproof: For a fixed attainable subspace, the squared norm of the orthogonal projection is the maximum squared fidelity. This full subproof is reused.
neighbors.proof_difference: T3 starts with a supplied prefix partition and projects onto vectors constant on each leaf, then derives refinement and variance estimates. Here the subspaces are coordinate spans selected by time-ordered contacts. Proving attainability and optimizing those spans over child/time assignments is the main work.

neighbors.shared_subproof: Both consider information that remains below a rooted node with limited further depth.
neighbors.proof_difference: T2 propagates Bernstein differences through two fixed branches and bounds a raw sample error. These children compete for contact times and carry arbitrary vertex weights.

neighbors.shared_subproof: Both optimize squared fidelity over a family and require achievable extremizers.
neighbors.proof_difference: B3n optimizes over Bell-sector probability distributions under two measured means. These constraints instead come from when real rotations can reach tree vertices; the sharp value requires scheduling and signed synthesis.

neighbors.shared_subproof: Both preserve signed amplitudes under a real rotation.
neighbors.proof_difference: B1n gives two specified gates and classifies a two-qubit ray. This item constructs matching layers on arbitrary finite trees.

candidates.shared_subproof: A first contact across a tree edge opens one new coordinate for future layers. Extracted contacts bound all reachable support and also give a reversible way to synthesize amplitudes on the reached sites. Projection and scheduling are separate inputs to sharpness.
candidates.decisive_difference: Compute the maximum squared fidelity attainable from a fixed tree root by a specified number of disjoint two-site rotation layers. The new work characterizes dynamic support, assigns child starting times, and proves its fidelity upper bound is attainable for signed amplitudes.
candidates.full_credit_work: Bound arbitrary circuits by the coordinates reachable along time-ordered contacts, construct signed states on the chosen coordinates, join this with the sharp projection bound, solve the child scheduling problem by a polynomial dynamic program, and certify all requested depths on a tree where radius alone overstates fidelity.

candidates.family_group: Monomial unitaries on labeled permutation cycles
candidates.assessment_overlap: The public v2 permutation_heisenberg_pullback family shares the pullback of a diagonal quantity, and coherent_control_global_relative_phase shares the need for one common phase. The v3 extension inherits the v2 comparisons and adds promise_register_protocols. The public controlled_permutation_semantics pilot tests order, inverse and reindexing for phase-free SELECT. The sparse public family banded_sparse_address_semantics shares the input-routing convention. These are related foundations for the proposed training item.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: W0 follows a basis label through controlled routing and W1 assigns a complex weight to an input column.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: W0 constructs a two-sided inverse for phase-free SELECT. W1 uses selector probabilities, clean entries and per-slot bounds. C1s moves one diagonal gate through one full-system permutation, tests the uncorrected rewrite and exhibits an interference witness.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: B1n keeps the roles of control and target distinct and H1 follows the effect of multiplying an operator by a complex phase.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: B1n classifies entanglement after a rotation and controlled NOT. H1 rephases a Hermitian decomposition. C1s computes the input table required to commute two gates and locates the angles at which an unchanged table passes.

candidates.shared_subproof: BE111 supplies chronological multiplication for unweighted permutations. LA013 conjugates circuits by a wire relabeling, BE104 checks an omitted program-global phase, LA016 tests equality up to a scalar, and BE110 fixes the same selector throughout inversion. LA007 reads superposition amplitudes from columns. Workbook B2 corrects known branch phases on retained labels, P1 implements a phase table by kickback and B4 transports data under reversal. The reserved sparse-oracle and tensor-conjugation contracts concern different target operations.
candidates.decisive_difference: The intermediate label changes which phase multiplies each column. The task demands a necessary and sufficient global test for leaving an arbitrary table in place, an exact two-bit calibration for all angles, and a superposition witnessing the failure of the uncorrected order. A phase-free permutation product alone cannot supply those results.
candidates.admission_decision: Propose an uncounted D2 starting item within the shared C1s–C3s study family. Preserve the pullback and relative-phase exposure links across any future split. The comparisons cover the resolved 198 retained contracts, the 15 historical reservations, 18 workbook entries, public assessment family records and pilot, and all 7 plus 6 questions in the two preceding public deliveries.
candidates.full_credit_work: Act on one basis ket to obtain weight \(a(x)b(p(x))\) and label \(q(p(x))\). Identify \(g=f\circ p\) and prove uniqueness. Give both directions of the exact orbit-invariance test and the single-constant test for \(f(p(x))/f(x)\), with a fixed sign convention for that constant. On two bits compute the table \(e^{i\theta(t\oplus c)}\), use the fixed control-zero columns to fix any common phase, and use a moved column to identify all angles. At \(\theta=\pi\) propagate a normalized two-term input through both orders, establish orthogonality, and explain equality of the basis-input output probabilities.

candidates.family_group: Monomial unitaries on labeled permutation cycles
candidates.assessment_overlap: Public v2 permutation_heisenberg_pullback and coherent_control_global_relative_phase separate a relabeling from the phase attached to a coherent branch. The internal_bond_phase_interference family supplies related phase sensitivity. The v3 extension inherits the v2 cohort. The public controlled_permutation_semantics pilot studies inverse routing and reindexing on preserved registers. It provides no criterion for compatibility of pinned vertex phases around a labeled physical cycle.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: Both packets model a permutation route by a complex number attached to its input column, and W2 compares phases on colliding routes.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: W1 and W2 combine different routes into a clean matrix entry and optimize or certify a budget. C2s compares two devices on the same labeled route by constructing a single diagonal change of basis compatible with prescribed reference values.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: H1 follows rephasing explicitly, H2 checks compatibility of independently supplied data, and B2n diagnoses underdetermined complex data.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: C2s constrains a phase at every directed edge by the reference phases at its two ends. The coupled conditions run along orbit arcs and close around a cycle. The prior tasks use one common scalar, Pauli-block consistency and measurement of a single coherence, respectively.

candidates.shared_subproof: Plan313 classifies plain permutations under relabeling. BE108 and LA013 explicitly conjugate under a basis permutation, while BE111 fixes chronological order. BE104 and LA016 distinguish an overall phase from exact matrix equality. The reserved Plan305 concerns tensor-factor permutation conjugation and its coefficients. Workbook C2 cancels neighboring gauges on a tensor train with fixed endpoints, B2 corrects relative phases in one output, and B4 uses a fixed relabeling. Cycle closure and consistency of several external phase references are new obligations here.
candidates.decisive_difference: The allowed conjugation is diagonal and labels stay fixed. An unconstrained match requires one oriented product per cycle. Prescribed phases add constraints along arcs in that cycle, and the construction must recover every calibrating diagonal including its componentwise freedom. Two prescribed phases can obstruct an otherwise valid match.
candidates.admission_decision: Propose an uncounted D3 transfer item in the same exposure family as C1s and C3s. The graph anchors establish weighted basis action and composition. The labeled-cycle classification and fixed-reference extension are authored deductions. Comparison covers the 198 retained contracts, 15 historical reservations, 18 workbook entries, public assessment family records and pilot, and all 7 plus 6 questions in the preceding deliveries.
candidates.full_credit_work: Derive the edge equation \(d_{p(x)}=(b_x/a_x)d_x\). Prove full-cycle consistency and compatibility of reference ratios with products of \(b_x/a_x\) along forward arcs. Show the cycle products classify an unpinned labeled cycle under diagonal conjugation, construct the phases from a base choice for each cycle, and show that every solution is obtained. An unpinned cycle has one free unit scalar, and a compatible pinned cycle has none. Include one reference, several references and fixed points. Construct two candidate devices with equal cycle products but inconsistent prescribed endpoints on a single cycle, and identify the specific failing arc.

candidates.proposed_use: Public study/proposed-training candidate. Official split unassigned.
candidates.family_group: Monomial unitaries on labeled permutation cycles
candidates.assessment_overlap: The public v2 permutation_heisenberg_pullback family transports a quantity under a basis permutation, and internal_bond_phase_interference concerns coherent phase information lost by some observations. The v3 public extension adds promise_register_protocols. The controlled_permutation_semantics pilot studies phase-free products and inverses. Our repeated powers use the composition substrate, but the observations here are complex traces of a known routing pattern with unknown edge phases.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: Complex routes can give ambiguous aggregate observations. W1 distinguishes the aggregate clean entry from its per-slot values, and W2 checks when a column sum reveals a full cap budget.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: C3s deals with characteristic factors of repeated orbits and power traces of a single unitary, then recovers products through divisibility or from measurements resolved by cycle length. The six-label ambiguity even preserves the full spectrum.

prior_public_neighbors.shared_subproof: H3 uses observations resolved by auxiliary eigenspace, B2n reconstructs a complex parameter from measurements, and B3n asks what observables leave undetermined.
prior_public_neighbors.decisive_difference: C3s derives an inverse problem for traces of powers. It must detect a polynomial collision across cycle lengths, invert a triangular system for distinct lengths, and recover repeated roots from sector power sums. Neither an affine Hamiltonian fit nor parity-state tomography supplies these steps.

candidates.shared_subproof: Plan108 uses trace invariance, Plan109 recovers representation multiplicities from a full character, and Plan313 groups unweighted permutations by cycle length. Plan415 estimates a density spectrum with symmetry restrictions. BE111 and BE110 implement phase-free routes. Reserved Plan219 distinguishes taking ordinary powers from transforming singular values. Workbook P1 uses a particular eigenvector of a cyclic shift; B2 distinguishes relative phases through coherent readout; C3 computes inner-product data through a recurrence. None of those recovery problems assigns independent edge products to labeled cycles from powers of one unknown matrix.
candidates.decisive_difference: The data aggregate all lengths in each power. Distinct cycle lengths admit recursive labeled recovery even with divisibility. Repeated lengths can even conceal changes to the multiset at a given length. Length-resolved reports recover each multiset with multiplicity, while any unequal products within a length still allow assignments to different labels.
candidates.admission_decision: Propose an uncounted D4 transfer item and keep the C1s–C3s family linked for exposure. The cycle trace formula, spectral factorization and inverse problems are authored deductions from the weighted composition law. Comparison covers 198 retained contracts, 15 historical reservations, 18 workbook entries, public assessment family records and pilot, and all 7 plus 6 preceding public questions.
candidates.full_credit_work: Iterate the basis action and separate fixed labels of a power from nonreturning labels. Show that a length-\(\ell\) orbit contributes \(z^\ell-h_C\) to \(\det(zI-U)\) and contributes \(\ell h_C^{n/\ell}\) to \(t_n\) only when \(\ell\mid n\). For distinct lengths recover the product on the unique length-\(\ell\) cycle from \(t_\ell\) after subtracting all shorter divisor contributions, including the base case. With two fixed points and two transpositions, realize two assignments by unit phases and verify a common characteristic polynomial or equality of every trace, together with different within-length multisets. For the augmented observations, divide length-resolved traces by \(\ell\), use the first \(m_\ell\) power sums to reconstruct the monic polynomial of cycle products and all root multiplicities. Show that within-length permutations of products leave the reports invariant, and characterize unique labeled assignment for each length, including the cases of one cycle or identical products.
